answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The copper multiplier is published, charged in knoll, and tide lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2390 identities would post 3416 proofs and burn roughly 34 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
